source: Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council — Winter Service Plan 2024/2025

fleet.note: One regular truck + driver assigned per route (10 routes : 10 trucks). Section 3.2/3.4.1, p.21-22.

timing.note: "A treatment run for each gritting truck would typically take approximately 2 hours to complete. Gritting normally take place at 7pm and/or 5am, depending on the weather conditions." p.11-12 (section 1.9).

saltStock.note: Minimum stock = 20 full treatments of the entire 10-route network at max spread rate. Section 3.5.4.

spreadRateMatrix_gPerM2.note: DLR's own Precautionary Treatment matrix (section 4.2.2) — target dry-salt spread rate by forecast Road Surface Temperature (RST), 'Good' spreader capability. Winter Watch's code picks the band from the live forecast's 2m temperature as a proxy for RST (see FLAGS-LOG) and shows this exact table as the citation.

decisionGuide.note: Qualitative guidance from section 4.2.1 (Decision Matrix Guide), used by the AI only to EXPLAIN the code's verdict, never to decide it.
points: Salt before frost when the road is dry, damp or wet and frost is expected.
Hoar frost is hardest to time: salt deposited too early on a dry road can disperse before it takes effect; ideally treat as the frost is forming.
If rain is freezing on contact with the road, this is the most serious condition and requires full precautionary treatment even on dry roads.
Salt is ineffective in the short term below -7°C; abrasives should be used instead when temperatures are expected to stay below -7°C for long periods.
